findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted.

1) The junction between the wall and left side of the sink in the women’s bathroom was observed to have a crack in the caulking that is providing a gap. 2) The caulk around the sink in the men’s bathroom was observed cracking and providing a gap. The PIC was notified and instructed to repair prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all hand sinks have smooth and easily cleanable surfaces sealing them to the walls moving forward.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(3) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (3) Cleaning equipment and utensils as specified under 4-602.11(A) and sanitizing as specified under § 4-703.11.

Multiple pieces of ice in the ice machine are observed with black and brown spots on them. The PIC was shown and instructed to have the machine cleaned/serviced. They called their technician during this inspection, and they said that they would be here before noon to conducted maintenance. Bagged ice is being acquired for the short term to correct. The PIC will contact the inspector and a spot check conducted to ensure that the machine is providing safe food.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The bottom of the ice bin behind the bar is observed with debris in it alongside and intermixed with the ice. The PIC was shown and cleaned the bin during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

The inside of the microwave is observed soiled with food splash during this inspection. The PIC was directed to clean and maintain clean at all times. Ensure that all non-food contact surfaces are cleaned and sanitized regularly to prevent possible ready to eat food contamination.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment, and linens: properly stored, dried, and handled.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

A container of utensils in the kitchen is observed with a soiled inner bottom. The PIC was shown and moved the container and utensils to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact surfaces are stored so that they are protected from contamination until use.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

On arrival the hand sink in the bar area had run out of soap. New soap was supplied during this inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that hand sinks remain fully supplied at all times.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

This facility does not a CFPM available at the facility at the time of this inspection. The PIC has a certificate for completing the course for the CFPM but not the certification for completing the test. They are instructed to complete the test prior to the next routine inspection and maintained a copy of the certificate at this facility. Biscuits and gravy were prepared and served this morning and the dishes are still observable in the kitchen during this inspection.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

The middle standing freezer in the back area appears to have been left cracked open last night at closing. Multiple items throughout the freezer (including pre-cooked chicken tenders, beef patties and mozzarella sticks) are observed thawed and with temperatures ranging from 46F-54F. These items were discarded by the PIC during this inspection. The rest of the items in the freezer are observed to be either still frozen or within acceptable cold holding temperatures. The freezer was closed tightly to allow for effective functioning of the unit. Ensure that the TCS foods are maintained cold at all times when not cooked or hot holding.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

At the start of this inspection there sani buckets were not prepared and ready for use. Education was conducted and the bucket made during this inspection to correct. Ensure that sanitizers are available for use at all times that food handling operations (including ice) are taking place.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The fan cover in the walk in cooler is heavily soiled during this inspection. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean regularly to prevent accumulation of dust/filth.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
6-403.11: (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES cannot occur. 

A container of lasagna is observed in the kitchen cooler. This appears to be (and is confirmed to be) an employee food that is being stored with foods intended for consumers. Education was conducted and the container discarded during this inspection to correct. A cooler is designated for employee foods in the back of the facility and should be used by all employees moving forward.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and then turn off the faucet with their bare hands. Education conducted. Ensure that proper hand washing is taking place at all times.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

The primary breakfast maker at this facility does not have a Certified Food Protection Manager Certificate. On asking they brought out a Certificate of Completion for the training. This sheet warns that this is not the certification and only prepares for the certification test. The PIC is instructed to continue and take/pass the certification test and maintain a copy of the certification moving foreword.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.115: (A) Live animals may not be allowed on PREMISES of a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT (B) Live animals may be allowed on PREMISE under certain conditions if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES does not occur. (C) Live or dead FISH bait may be stored if contamination of FOOD and FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES is prevented. 

1) A small dog was observed on the bar counter at the beginning of the inspection. 2) A large dog is observed to be walking around the facility (including through the kitchen) during this inspection. Both dogs were removed during this inspection prior to a conversation taking place with the PIC. That conversation did take place before the end of the inspection. Pets should not be allowed in the facility and especially should not be allowed in the food service areas of the facility.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

The primary breakfast maker at this facility does not have a Certified Food Protection Manager Certificate. A CFPM arrived during this inspection to correct the immediate violation. It was discussed that any time that food handling or preparation (beyond heating up in a microwave or oven) is taking place, a CFPM needs to be on site. Options discussed included having the breakfast person taking the course/test, pre making the breakfast sandwiches or adjusting the schedule so that CFPMs are on the morning shift. Hand outs were given during this inspection for the current known CFPM courses in this area.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

An employee was observed to wash hands and then turn off the faucet with their bare hands. Employee then proceded to handle the ice scoop in the bar. Education conducted. Ensure that proper hand washing is taking place at all times.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The metal deflector shield in the ice machine is soiled. PIC was directed to it and the item was cleaned during this inspection to correct. Ensure that this is maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The hand sink and stand in the bathroom appear to be pulling away from the wall. Repair prior to the next routine inspection. Also ensure that it is sealed to the wall so that it provides a smooth and easily cleanable surface.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Container of horseradish mustard stored on ambient temperature shelves in the kitchen. Manufacturer label indicates “refrigerate after opening.” CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who voluntarily discarded the item. Store foods as indicated by manufacturer.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
-Open gallon of milk observed without date-marking. CORRECTED- PIC labeled milk with the date it was opened. Label all refrigerated TCS foods with the date opened. Use or discard within 7 days. Do not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date.
-Coleslaw labeled 11/17 observed in the kitchen fridge. CORRECTED- PIC voluntarily discarded. Use or discard food within 7 days of preparation.
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date. [Pf]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Frost accumulation observed in the middle storage freezer. Defrost/clean to eliminate frost accumulation so that interior is smooth & easily cleanable.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be safe. P Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Bare plywood observed in the bar area behind/under the 3 compartment sink. Seal or cover plywood so that it is no longer absorbent and is smooth & easily cleanable. PIC is in the process of getting bids to paint/seal the area.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Soda nozzle observed with soil build up. CORRECTED- Washed rinsed and sanitized. Maintain clean to sight and touch.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
One dozen-pack of shell eggs observed at 48-50F (surface temperature). CORRECTED- Eggs voluntarily discarded. Another box of eggs in the same cooler observed at 38F with ice on the bottom of the box. Discussed monitoring and adjusting temperature as needed.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Bare plywood observed in the bar area behind/under the 3 compartment sink. Seal or cover plywood so that it is no longer absorbent and is smooth & easily cleanable.
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. [C]

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
PIC is in the process of CFM training but is not yet certified. 
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: Raw shell eggs and raw hamburger observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (cheese and citrus fruits in the lowest drawers) in the kitchen fridge. CORRECTED— Since no foods appear to be contaminated, storage rearranged to prevent potential contamination. Provided education on proper storage to prevent contamination
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Several violations observed regarding food and non-food contact surfaces:
— Cloths observed in food contact uses in the following locations: 1) covering a food prep surface; 2) draped over taco pizza ingredients; and 3) in a bag of tomatoes. Cease use of cloths in contact with food.
— Knife block observed for storage of knives in the kitchen. Cease use as the interior (that is in contact with the knife blades) is not easily cleanable.
— Wood cutting board observed in use in the kitchen. Wood is not smooth or easily cleanable. Cease use.
4-101.11: (A) Materials used for FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES may not allow migration of deleterious substances shall be: (B) Durable, nonabsorbent, and CORROSION-RESISTANT (C) Sufficient in weight and thickness (D) SMOOTH, EASILY CLEANABLE surface (E) Resistant to pitting, chipping, scratching, decomposition, and distortion. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Walls (plywood) and floors where the meat slicer is located are not smooth/easily cleanable, and therefore not a suitable environment for food handling. Repair so that surfaces are smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. [C]

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.comment:
Sunglasses and a cigarillo observed stored among the spices in the kitchen. CORRECTED— Items were removed. Store personal items away from food prep and storage.
6-501.110: (A) Dressing rooms shall be used by EMPLOYEES if the EMPLOYEES regularly change their clothes in the establishment. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be used for the orderly storage of EMPLOYEE clothing and other possessions. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
No employee health documents are on file. Inspector emailed necessary form— print one out for each employee to sign.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD.  [Pf]

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
No written vomit/diarrhea clean up policy available. Inspector emailed a
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. [Pf]

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.comment:
Facility (with a medium risk permit) has prepared and cooled foods to be reheated for service at another time. These activities are not allowed under a medium risk permit. Inspector provided education. To continue cooling and reheating foods, facility must upgrade to a high risk permit. CORRECTED— Foods prepared outside of the current permit must be discarded.
3-201.11: (A) FOOD shall be obtained from sources that comply with LAW. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Raw shell eggs observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (cheese sauce, cheese slices, citrus fruit) in the kitchen fridge. CORRECTED— Since no foods appear to be contaminated, storage rearranged to prevent potential contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Cl rinse in the bar 3 compartment sink observed at 25ppm. CORRECTED— Remade sanitizer to correct concentration.
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Bar 3 compartment sink observed set up to wash, sanitize, then rinse dishes. This eliminates the sanitize step, so dishes are not being sanitized. CORRECTED— Provided education. Staff set up sink to wash, rinse, then sanitize, and discussed the need to air-dry.
4-703.11: After cleaning, FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be SANITIZED in: (A) manual hot water operations. (B) mechanical hot water operations. (C) Chemical manual or mechanical operations. Contact times shall be consistent with those on EPA-registered label use – standard contact time 30 seconds. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Foods observed past the 7 day date marking. In the kitchen fridge, cheese sauce dated 11/10, chili dated 11/4, and coleslaw dated 11/4. Sausage gravy in the kitchen cooler observed without any date marking. CORRECTED— Foods without date marking or 7 days past their date marking must be discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Foods and single service items observed stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Store items at least 6 inches above the floor to protect from potential contamination.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. [C]

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Ice scoop in the bar ice bin observed stored with handle in contact with the ice. Store scoop so that ice may be scooped without bare hand contact with the ice.
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed food basket in hand sink at the bar. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated ice is periodically dumped in the hand sink. Cease practice. Discussed that the hand sink is for hand washing ONLY. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed raw chicken breast to be correctly stored on bottom shelf of the kitchen refrigerator; however, shred cheese bags were placed directly on top of raw chicken storage. Cease practice. Inspector moved cheese during inspection. COS. Discussed with PIC.

Observed shell eggs to be store above RTE sauces and tortillas at the back refrigerator. Incorrect storage order. Shell eggs should not be stored above ready-to-eat foods. Cease practice. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:

If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment: Colander was sitting in the bar handwashing sink at the beginning of the inspection. Hand washing sinks must be accessible at all times. CORRECTED- Colander was removed.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (Pf)

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Lettuce stored below a plastic container of raw fish. Store Ready-To-Eat foods above raw to protect from cross-contamination. CORRECTED- PIC discarded fish, rearranged storage for food protection/prevention of contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11 (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables. (P)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Date marking is not on heavy cream in the bar 3 door cooler; coleslaw in the kitchen fridge. CORRECTED- Employee voluntarily discarded heavy cream. PIC marked coleslaw with the date the package was opened.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17 Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). (Pf)

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment: Test kits or other devices are not available to the employees to measure sanitizing solution concentration. Provide a test kit or other measuring device so the employees can measure concentrations and ensure proper sanitization. Avoid a concentration of sanitizer that is too high, which can be toxic.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. (Pf)

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment: The restrooms do not have self-closing doors. Provide closers on restroom doors.
findings.citation_text: 6-202.14 All toilet rooms located within a food establishment must be enclosed with a tight-fitting and self-closing door. (C)

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment: Floor in the dry storage area were found in a state of disrepair (hole in the floor, covered by plywood).
findings.citation_text: 6-201.11 Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable. (C)

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed tomatoes in the refrigerator to not be in sound condition and without date marking. The tomatoes had begun to spoil and it is unsure when they were cut. Ensure that PHFs, specifically tomatoes, are date marked with the date they were cut. Tomatoes were discarded during the inspection. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Cross-contamination, equipment, personnel, storage
findings.comment:
Observed beer being stored in the ice machine. The ice machine contains ice that will be used for service in drinks. The ice the beer was in was scooped out and discarded. Ensure that no items are stored in the ice chest that is intended for drinks. 
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed eggs in the refrigerator to be being stored over produce. Eggs are a raw product and should be stored below ready to eat food. Eggs were discarded the inspection. 
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the soda gun to have an excessive accumulation of soda debris on it. Ensure that the soda gun is cleaned at regular intervals to prevent a potential for cross contamination. Soda gun cleaned during the inspection. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the shelving units in the rear of the facility to have some amounts of mice droppings on them. Some areas of the baseboards were noted to have been chewed on. No other evidence of pest infestations were noted. Ensure that the shelving units are cleaned. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
Observed the facility to not have hand soap at the hand sink at the bar. Hand soap was provided. No self-closers noted on the restrooms. Provide the restrooms with the self-closers. 
750-1120e A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed hot dogs in the fridge to be open with several missing and no date marking noted. Ensure that PHFs that are ready to eat are date marked with the day they were opened and discarded after 7 days. Employee stated she was going to discard the hot dogs.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potentially hazardous foods properly thawed
findings.comment:
Observed four bags of mozzarela cheese in the 3 compartment sink in the kitchen to be thawing. There was no running water noted. Employee was notified of proper methods for thawing. Employee began running water of the cheese for proper thawing procedures. 
750-240 Potentially hazardous foods shall be properly thawed by one of the  following method. 1. Under refrigeration 41°F or below, 2. Under  potable running water 70°F or below or below with sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose food particles into the over-flow, 3. In microwave as part of the cooking process, 4. As part of the cooking process.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the pizza oven, on the inside, to have a thick accumulation of food debris. Ensure that food contact surfaces are regularly washed, rinsed, and sanitized. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment:
1) Observed utensils in the kitchen stored in a bucket with the food surface side sticking out. This does not allow for proper handling of utensils, since they can not be taken out of the bucket from the non-food contact area. Invert the utensils so that the food contact side is protected. 2) Observed clean cutting boards resting on the floor. Ensure that equipment is stored at least 6 inches off the floor. 
750-850 Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.
750-860 Cleaned and sanitized utensils an equipment shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in a clean, dry location in a way that protects them from contamination by splash, dust and other means.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed a bucket under the three compartment sink at the bar that was filled with hazy water and overflowing onto the floor. It appears to be coming from a leak under the three compartment sink. Ensure that waste water is disposed of regularly to avoid pest infestations. Employee emptied the bucket during the insepction.
750-1050 All water containing sewage shall be disposed of  properly either by a public sewage system or an approved private disposal system which is constructed and operated in conformance with applicable State and local laws, ordinances and regulations.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed a leak from the PVC piping under the ice bin. Plumbing should be maintained to not allow leaks to avoid waste water accumulation. Ensure that the plumbing is repaired by an Illinois licensed plumber. 
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed the walk-in keg cooler floor to be separated from the wall. This has led to the exposure of the ground underneath the facility. Ensure that the walk-in floor is repaired to not allow visible ground beneath the flooring. 
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
1) Observed oven cleaner and bleach sitting alongside a shelf stable butter on a shelf. 2) Observed mulitple cleaners sitting next to liquors at the liquor holder at the bar. Ensure that chemicals are stored below and away from food, food products, and drinks. Employee moved the chemicals during the inspection.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Premises maintained fee of litter, unnecessary articles. Cleaning and maintaining equipment properly...
findings.comment:
Observed an oven in the kitchen that was excessively dirty with food splash and debris. When the oven was opened grease began to drip from around the oven door and inside the oven. When employee was asked about the oven it was stated that the oven was not in service and had not been in service since the most recent owners took over (2014). Employee also noted it was not hooked up to the gas line or electricity. Remove all items that are unnecessary for the operation of the business.
750-1350c Only articles necessary for the operation and maintenance of the food service establishment shall be stored on the premises.  Remove all unnecessary items.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed mouse dropping on a shelf in the dry storage. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are in good repair and maintained in a clean manner. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed mouse droppings on a shelf in the back storage area. Ensure that proper cleaning is being done, especially with a known rodent problem. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed mouse droppings that appeared both fresh and old on the floors in back storage area, by the desk, and dropping on the shelf with single-service items. Employee was unable to provide documentation or invoice that AAA had been out for the rodent issue following last complaint inspection. No visible traps were noted.
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed mouse droppings near the desk in the back and on the floor of the dry storage area. Ensure that proper cleaning is being done, especially with a known rodent problem. 
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed a container of soiled batter used for previous weeks fish fry. Remove this item and wash, rinse, and sanitze after each use. Do not re-use old container without being properly washed.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Proper hygienic practices, eating/drinking/smoking (evidence)
findings.comment:
Observed ash trays stored behind the bar. Investigation of complaint for smoking was unfounded, however, evidence was observed. Ash trays were discarded to correct the violation
750-530c Employees may use tobacco in any form only in designated areas. Areas shall not be designated for that purpose if the use of tobacco might result in the contamination of food, equipment, utensils or other items needing protection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed the flat top grill in the back to be soiled with grease and other accumulated debris. Ensure that food contact surfaces are washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use. 
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the shelving soiled with new and old mice droppings in the dry storage area. Ensure that non-food contact surfaces are cleaned so that they are free of dust, dirt, and debris. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment:
Observed a mop bucket with soiled water in the back storage area with the chest freezers. Also, observed a bucket underneath the 3 compartment sink full of soiled water. Ensure that waste water is emptied following use. 
750-1130(e) Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment: Observed the men's restroom to be without a covered trash can. Both restrooms were observed to have their self closers deattached. Ensure that both restrooms have covered trash cans and self-closing doors.  750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms. 750-1110d Toilet facilities shall be kept clean and in good repair and free of objectionable odors. A supply of toilet tissue shall be provided at each toilet at all times. Easily cleanable, covered receptacles shall be provided for waste materials.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
Observed old and new mouse droppings throughout the storage area of the facility. Ensure that appropriate measure are being taken to avoid pest infestations. 
750-1160 Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Toxic items properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed a bottle of kitchen degraser improperly stored on top of the pizza oven. Store all toxic chemicals away from food storage and food equipment. Bottle was removed to its proper location to correct the violation.
750-1310 All toxic items must be properly stored (i.e. segregated from food) to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all chemicals.

findings.title: Clean and soiled linen segregated and properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed multiple rags throughout the facility that appeared to be soiled and not in a covered container. Ensure soiled rags are stored in proper containers until removed from the facility. 
750-1380b Soiled clothes and linens shall be stored in non-absorbent containers or washable laundry bags until removed for laundering. Properly store soiled linens.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment: 750-140b Observed contents of the kitchen refrigerator to not have any date marking. Coleslaw, tuna salad, mozzarella cheese, need to be dated with the date they are opened. Potentially hazardous, ready-to-eat foods should be used within seven days.  Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
750-250 Observed diced tomatoes being stored in a reused coleslaw container resting on the counter. Foods were probed and found to be 56F. Discussed handling with employee. Facility opted to use time as control. Tomatoes will be cut and used within four hours. Food will be used or discarded after lunch.   All potentially hazardous foods shall be kept at 41°F or below while on display and service.
750-151(a) Observed bulk cheese slices and tuna salad opened without date and present in cooler for several days. Employee stated that normally, only a small portion is kept in the refrigerator and the bulk is kept in the freezer until needed. That is a good practice. To avoid having cheese in the kitchen longer than seven days, portion smaller amounts and keep the majority in the freezer.  Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment: 750-130(d) Observed a thoroughly soiled batter bucket stored on the lower shelf of the steam table. This container should be removed from service for cleaning once batter becomes caked onto surfaces. The batter should be sifted through daily and replaced weekly. This container is thickly coated with batter and food debris. Wash, rinse, and sanitize this container. All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed bag of cheese shreds and cheese slices to not be properly closed. Keep foods tightly wrapped and protected during non-service periods. In use foods may be kept opened. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
750-290 Ice scoop is observed being stored on top of a soiled ice machine. Clean the ice machine surface on a daily basis or store the clean scoop in a clean container. Cease storing food utensils on soiled surfaces.  Ice scoop shall be stored on a clean surface or in the ice with the handle extended out of the ice.
750-280 Observed an in-use stirring spoon soiled and stored on a clean plate by the taco meat. Store spoon in food or keep track of the time on the plate - four hour rule.  Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750-510a Observed employee rinse hands and turn off water without properly washing and using a paper towel to turn off faucet. Properly wash hands with soap and then dry hands with a paper towel. Use the paper towel to turn off the water faucet so that hands are not contaminated by soiled faucet. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time their hands may have become contaminated and prior to handling food or clean equipment.
750-1120e A soiled common towel is observed being hung on the drawer handle beneath the cash register. Cease use of the common towel.   Hand-cleansing soap shall be available at each lavatory. Sanitary towels or a heated air hand-drying device shall be conveniently located near each lavatory. Common towels are prohibited. If disposable towels are provided a waste receptacle shall be conveniently located near the hand washing facilities.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment: 750-690 There is unsealed wood on the shelves of the bar holding some of the bottled liquor. Employee stated that new shelving is being installed/built and then the entire surface will be sealed again. Keep the bare wood smooth and easily cleanable. Also, the mini fridge of the bar has frost accumulation at the freezer portion. Defrost the mini-fridge.  Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Wiping cloths clean, used properly, stored
findings.comment: 750-810b Bar is open for food and alcohol service and does not have a proper sani-bucket or spray bottle of sanitizer available. Provide a bucket or bottle filled with 100ppm bleach solution for the cleaning of counters.  Moist cloths used for wiping food spills on kitchenware and food-contact surfaces shall be clean and rinsed frequently in one of the permitted sanitizing solutions. See Section 750.820e.   These cloths shall be stored in a proper sanitizing solution between uses.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment: 750-800(b) Observed the following food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) grill top and surrounding surface of this equipment; 2) fryer adjacent to the grill flat top (both surfaces soiled with accumulated grease and food debris); 3) pizza over (old pizza cheese in drip tray); 4) pans stored in the base of the oven (grease and mouse droppings); 5) inside of the microwave (food), and 6) soda gun and catch cup (mold). The area around the grill has not been detail cleaned in an apparently significantly long time. There is thick grease accumulation along the sides and front of the knobs. Clean these aforementioned items. To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment: 750-800e The following non-food contact surfaces are observed soiled: 1) inside of the refrigerator in the kitchen (serious accumulation of food spills and splash); 2) fans throughout the kitchen - exhaust and oscillating are coated with dust (especially the exhaust fan in the back room); 3) fry baskets and rack in kitchen (grease and crumbs); and 4) sides of the ovens (grease). Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Storage/handling of clean equipment, utensils
findings.comment: 750-850 The cabinet to the right of the three compartment sink is stocked full of equipment and utensils that are soiled with dust and splash from washing activities. Remove these extra utensils for cleaning. Cleaned and sanitized equipment and utensils shall be handled in a way that protects them from contamination.  Spoons, knives and forks shall be touched only by their handles.  Cups glasses, bowls, plates and similar items shall be handled without contact with inside surfaces or with surfaces that contact the user’s mouth.

findings.title: Single service articles not re-used
findings.comment: 750-600 Observed a number of taco toppings being stored in Country Coleslaw plastic containers. The containers are cleaned before being used to hold onions, tomatoes, and lettuce. A Variance Request has been submitted to allow for this practice. Pending approval, this re-use of containers will be allowed. Re-use of single-service articles is prohibited. Do not re-use single service items.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.comment: 750-1130(e) There was observed two buckets of waste water from an old leak at the three compartment sink of the bar. Buckets of frothy, soiled liquid were discarded during the inspection. Liquid waste from compacting or cleaning operations shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment: 750-1120 The hot and cold water faucets are switched on the womens toilet room handsink. Properly change the faucets so they are correctly marked.  There is an individual hot water heater at this sink. Provide hot water for the handsink. Each lavatory shall be provided with hot and cold water tempered by means of a mixing valve or combination faucet.

findings.title: Hand washing sinks installed, located, accessible
findings.comment: 750-1110(a) Observed the kitchen to not have a proper handsink. The nearest handsink is on the far side of the bar and not close to the kitchen. There is a three compartment sink available at the kitchen. Food is not the primary service at this establishment. A Variance has been submitted to allow this kitchen to designate one of the three compartment sinks as a handwashing sink. This sink should be supplied with soap, paper toweling, and designated signage so staff know to wash hands at this sink. Toilet facilities for employees shall be provided and installed according to law, shall be conveniently located and shall be accessible to employees at all times.

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750-1120e Paper towels were not available at the sink with soap available in the kitchen. Provide soap and paper towels for the sinks in the kitchen. A supply of soap and and sanitary towels (or a hand drying device) shall be provided at each lavatory.
750-1120 Neither of the toilet rooms is provided a self closure for the door. Provide springs for both bathroom doors. Womens toilet room does not have a proper covered garbage can. Provide a covered garbage can. All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.

findings.title: Presence of insects/rodents.  Animals prohibited
findings.comment:
750-1160 Observed drain flies in the thickly coated catch cup of the bar soda gun. See violation #22. The gun and attached cup are observed soiled with accumulated molds and provided growth opportunities for the flies. The soda gun was cleaned and the catch cup was removed for cleaning during the inspection. Please clean the surrounding area of the soda gun to insure pest breeding grounds are eliminated. 
Observed mouse droppings within the cabinet of the women's toilet room. Gnaw marks and pieces of the cabinet have been chewed. The pests are observed around the water heater in that cabinet. Also, observed mouse droppings in the base drawer of the oven in the kitchen. Droppings are observed over the various pans being stored in this lower shelf. 
Effective measures to minimize the presence of rodents and insects shall be utilized. Provide effective pest control.

findings.title: Outer openings protected from insects, rodent proof
findings.comment: 750-1170 Observed the back door to not have a self-closer. See notes in General Comments. The door also has visible daylight around the top and edges. Some weather stripping has been applied. Continue adding weather stripping until daylight is no longer visible around the door. Openings to the outside shall be protected against the entrance of rodents and insects.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment: 750-1220 Bar floor has been resealed except for the corner under the soda syrup boxes. This area is observed soiled with debris from the weekend. The kitchen floor is observed soiled with grease and food crumbs in the gaps between equipment. Clean the kitchen floor paying attention to areas around equipment.  Floors shall be kept clean. Clean the floors.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment: 750-1210 The vent in the ceiling of the mens toilet room is opened. Replace/cover the open ceiling square in the mens room. All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.
Observed food storage bags in the upright freezer in the store room of sausage, pepperoni, and vegetables, that were not in their original packaging and not labeled with the time and date they were prepared. 
Label all potentially hazardous food with a label containing the date and time they were removed from the original package.
**Repeat Violation**

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.citation_text:
750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F
The following refrigeration units did not contain thermometers: 1) the refrigerator in the kitchen ( Both cooler and freezer compartment.), 2) the walk in beer cooler. 
Provide thermometers in all coolers that contain potentially hazardous food.
**Repeat Violation**

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.
The establishment could not locate test strips for testing sanitizing solutions. 
Provide test kits for checking sanitizing solutions. 
CORRECTED = Personnel went and obtained a test kit during the inspection.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.
Observed the following surfaces to be soiled: 1) the inside of the pizza warmer, 2) the inside of the microwave, 3) the lip of the ice deflector in the ice machine.
Clean this equipment as necessary.
**Repeat Violation**

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Observed that the following surfaces were soiled: 1) The front and sides of the grille, 2) the front and sides of the fryer, and 3) the outside of the microwave. 
Clean these areas as necessary.
**Repeat Violation**

findings.title: Restrooms with self-closing doors, fixtures operate properly, facility clean, supplied with hand soa...
findings.comment:
750-1120 All restrooms must have self-closing doors, properly operating fixtures, be clean and have proper hand washing supplies in order to help facilitate good hygienic practices.  Provide properly designed and maintained restrooms.
Observed that the self- closing mechanisms (springs) for the rest room doors are inoperable (springs have been unhooked).
Repair self-closing mechanisms. 
CORRECTED = Springs were reattach to the doors.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. 
Observed that there are some floor tiles that are cracked in the store room near the chest freezers
Repair these tiles.
Observed that the floor under the fryer and grille are soiled with grease and some food spillage.
Clean the floors.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed containers and bags of food, including breaded chicken, fries, onion rings, and vegetables, that were not in their original packaging. These containers were not labeled with a date they were removed from the original package. 
750-140b Potentially hazardous food shall be labeled or tagged with date and time of preparation and rapidly cooled to an internal temperature of 41°F.
Label containers of foods not in their original packages with the date product was opened.
Observed a bulk container of flour that was not labeled as to the identity of the product.
750-130f Unless its identity is unmistakable, bulk food such as cooking oil, syrup, salt, sugar or flour not stored in the product container or package in which it was obtained, shall be stored in a container identifying the food by common name. Label bulk container with common name.

findings.title: Thermometers provided and conspicuously placed
findings.comment: Observed that the following cooling units did not contain thermometers: 1) refrigerator in kitchen, 2) chest freezer, 3) 2 door cooler in bar.
findings.citation_text:
750.140(a) All refrigeration units used to hold potentially hazardous foods shall contain a  conspicuously placed thermometer that is accurate to ±3°F. 
Provide thermometers in the above units.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment:
Observed that there was some personal / employee food items in the refrigerator in the kitchen. 
750-120a At all times, food shall be protected from potential contamination.
Store personal food items separately from commercial food items.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the inside of the pizza warmer, and the inside of the microwave is soiled.
Also observed that the lip of the ice deflector in the ice machine was moldy.
750-800d Food-contact surfaces of grills, griddles, and similar cooking devices and the cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least once a day.   The food-contact surfaces of all cooking equipment shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other accumulated soil.
Clean this equipment.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that the outside of the microwave oven, and the outside surfaces of the grille and fryer were soiled with grease build up. Also the handles of the cabinets under and across from the fryer were soiled with grease buildup. 
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.
Clean these areas as necessary.

findings.title: Floors properly constructed, clean, drained
findings.comment:
Observed that the floor under the shelves and cooking equipment in the kitchen were soiled. And the floor under the shelves and equipment in the store room were also soiled. 
750-1220 Floors shall be kept clean. 
Clean the floors.
Observed that the floor near the ice machine, and in the dry storage area had some cracked, broken, or missing tiles.
750-1200 All floors must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean floors.

findings.title: Lighting provided as required.  Fixtures shielded
findings.comment:
Observed that the light fixture in the area of the ice machine did not have a cover over the light bulb. 
750-1240 All lights in the food prep, food storage or kitchen area of a establishment must be properly shielded (i.e. either have a physical shield or be a shatter resistant bulb) so as to reduce the potential for cross contamination in case of breakage. 
 Provide properly shielded lights.
**REPEAT VIOLATION**
